- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of forecast horizon).
- Forecasts show upward trend bias, often overshooting true values by 2–5% in the first 10–15 days.
- After a spike in true values (e.g., 80+), model tends to overreact and continue rising, failing to peak and then decline as observed.
- Model underestimates true values in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, suggesting lag or mean reversion not captured.
- Forecasts are too smooth; fail to reflect sharp volatility or sudden drops in true values.
- Model exhibits “late correction” — true values often dip below forecast mid-to-late horizon, suggesting model doesn’t adjust for mean reversion or policy shocks.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 1–3% for the last 5–10 days of the horizon to align with observed mean reversion.
- Model tends to ignore recent true value drops (e.g., 80→75) and continues upward, indicating poor lag response to recent data.
